intent: cars wait before properly checkered starting bands in all three scenes

edits.purpose: Remove stripes from behind the cars; paint proper multirow checkerboards ahead of their front bumpers.
edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Edit target: the supplied square three-panel forest / desert / winter race poster.
Primary request: in ALL THREE scenes the car must be STOPPED BEFORE the starting line, and the starting line must be a PROPER BLACK-AND-WHITE CHECKERBOARD BAND.

CRITICAL CORRECTION: the current checkered stripes are BEHIND the rear wheels, so the cars have already crossed them. That is wrong. REMOVE those three old stripes completely, restoring the original road material beneath them. Then place ONE new correct checkerboard starting band per panel AHEAD OF THE CAR'S FRONT BUMPER in its direction of travel. The cars face AWAY from the viewer toward the upper-right background. AHEAD therefore means further up the road toward that background, never the foreground or below/behind the rear bumper. Each entire car, including front bumper and all four tyre contact points, is on the approach side of the line. There must be a clear strip of bare road between the nose and the nearest checkerboard edge, about half a metre in world space. No wheel, body, bumper or shadow should touch or overlap the band.

Keep each rear-three-quarter car's design, ivory/navy livery, straight wheels and road-aligned heading. You may move the car slightly toward the foreground/left and modestly adjust its size, or extend the immediate straight, if needed to make the relationship unmistakable. Do not crop any part of a car. The three scenes must clearly read: viewer -> rear of waiting car -> front/nose -> short visible bare-road gap -> CHECKERED START LINE -> open track continuing forward. The road must remain straight through the car and starting band, bending only beyond the line. No part of any old starting stripe remains behind or under any car.

Checkerboard construction: every starting band is a clean rectangular strip painted flat ACROSS the full road, with its long edge PERPENDICULAR to travel and parallel to the car's axles in world space. Use exactly THREE adjacent rows of evenly sized squares, roughly 12-16 columns across the road, all on ONE regular perspective grid. Adjacent cells alternate black/white in BOTH directions: row 1 BLACK WHITE BLACK WHITE; row 2 WHITE BLACK WHITE BLACK; row 3 BLACK WHITE BLACK WHITE. This is a real checkerboard with opposite colours in neighboring rows, NOT a single row of alternating rectangles, diagonal stripes, long bars, a zebra crossing, random triangles or checker-shaped shadows. The squares foreshorten consistently with the road plane. Keep the entire new band clearly readable ahead of each car.

Preserve exactly three equal horizontal scenic panels and thin navy dividers, top pine forest / middle warm DESERT WITH COMPACTED SAND ROAD / bottom winter snowbanks and asphalt. Preserve the three-lens amber starter boards, existing scenery and mature matte cel-shaded 3D style, crisp controlled shadow bands and natural palette. No asphalt conversion of the desert, no road centre dashes, arrows, extra flags, text, numbers, logos, branding, smoke or motion effects. Stationary straight cars, one per panel, correctly waiting behind their lines. Square 1:1 output.
edits.limitation: Bands remained too near the car silhouettes and partly occluded; refined before integration.

edits.purpose: Move all bands farther up the road, making the waiting position and full checkerboard visible.
edits.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Make ONE targeted correction to this three-panel race poster: move each of the THREE checkered starting bands FARTHER FORWARD along its road, so every waiting car is clearly and entirely BEFORE its starting band.

Keep the cars exactly where they are and keep their rear-three-quarter poses, size, wheels, livery and shadows. They face away toward the upper-right. The current bands are still too close to the nose and partly occluded by the cars. Remove every current starting band completely and restore road there. Repaint one band per panel MUCH FARTHER UP THE ROAD, with at least ONE FULL CAR LENGTH of visible bare road between the car's FRONT BUMPER and the NEAR EDGE of the band. The COMPLETE band must be visible, road-edge to road-edge, entirely beyond and clear of the silhouette of the car. Nothing on a car or its shadow can cover or touch a checker. The order is WAITING CAR -> CLEAR ROAD GAP -> STARTING BAND -> CONTINUING TRACK.

Placement guide for the 1254-square source, relative to each of the three approximately 418px-high panels: the car remains lower-left/foreground. Put the band in the open road toward the UPPER-RIGHT of that panel, roughly the 55%-65% height region, beyond the car's front, not along the bottom. Keep the new band wholly in the roadway. It should look smaller/farther away in perspective than the current band. You may straighten only the short road section at the band if needed so it crosses the starting straight at a right angle in world space. Do not move the stripe into the foreground or behind the rear wheels.

Preserve the proper checkerboard construction: exactly THREE neighboring rows of regular black and white squares; every horizontal AND vertical neighbor is the opposite colour, middle row inverted from the outer two rows. Uniform perspective grid, no zebra stripes, single-row bars, gaps, blobs or arbitrary quadrilaterals. Transverse band across full road width, squares foreshortened consistently with the road plane.
Keep all other parts of the image unchanged: exactly three equal horizontal panels, forest / compacted-sand desert / snowy winter, three amber lamps on each existing starter board, no road centre dashes, no text/numbers/logos, same mature matte cel-shaded 3D style, square 1:1 framing.

visual_review: Each car waits on the approach side, with a bare-road gap from its front bumper to the starting band.
No starting stripe remains under or behind a car.
Bands visibly alternate black and white across neighboring rows and columns on the road plane.
Forest, compacted-sand Desert and snowy Winter scenery, rear-quarter car views and three-lens starter boards remain.
reference_policy: Only project-generated original art is used. No external asset, manufacturer branding or runtime image provider.
